initial_plan.can_answer: partly: describes the annual reported number of pedestrians injured or killed in Brooklyn crashes, but not an exposure-adjusted safety risk or the cause of any change
initial_plan.metric: Annual pedestrian casualty count, calculated as the sum of number_of_pedestrians_injured plus number_of_pedestrians_killed across included Brooklyn crash rows
initial_plan.denominator: None; an annual count, not a rate
initial_plan.population: Police-reported crash rows with borough Brooklyn and a non-null crash_date in 2013 or later; each reported pedestrian injury or death contributes one casualty
initial_plan.years: Every calendar year from 2013 through the latest year represented by the file, subject to file coverage
initial_plan.data_check: Pending; inspect row coverage and only missingness in the two summed outcome columns before deciding how to treat missing outcomes.

data_check_interpretation.facts: The initial case-sensitive borough comparison returned no matching rows; normalizing borough with lower(trim()) produced 483,501 Brooklyn crash rows for 2013-2026. Among those rows, 0 had a missing/unknown borough or missing crash_date, and 0 had a null or negative number_of_pedestrians_injured or number_of_pedestrians_killed. Each full year from 2013 through 2025 had date coverage from January 1 through December 31; 2026 had 9,700 rows from January 1 through June 11 and is partial. Included full-year row counts range from 47,024 (2013) to 50,851 (2015) early in the series and 22,785 (2024) to 24,303 (2025) near its end.
data_check_interpretation.decisions: Changed the borough filter to case- and whitespace-normalized Brooklyn because the literal initial filter matched no rows. Keep all eligible 2013-2025 rows because neither summed outcome field has missing or impossible values in them. Exclude all 2026 rows (9,700) from the plotted trend because the file only covers that year through June 11; this changes the initial through-latest-year range to complete calendar years only.

final_plan.can_answer: partly: describes annual reported pedestrian casualty counts in Brooklyn crashes, but this crash file has no pedestrian, walking, traffic, or distance exposure denominator and cannot establish a change in pedestrian safety risk or its cause
final_plan.metric: For each calendar year, sum number_of_pedestrians_injured and number_of_pedestrians_killed across the selected crash rows; each reported injured or killed pedestrian contributes one casualty
final_plan.denominator: None; annual reported casualty count, not a rate
final_plan.population: Police-reported crash rows with lower(trim(borough)) = 'brooklyn' and crash_date in calendar years 2013-2025, inclusive; only complete calendar years are included
final_plan.years: 2013-2025 inclusive; the partial 2026 year is excluded
final_plan.limitations: This is an absolute count from police-reported crashes, not an exposure-adjusted risk or a measure of all pedestrian harm. Checks found 0 missing or negative values in either summed outcome field among the 2013-2026 Brooklyn check population; 2026 was only covered through June 11 (9,700 rows), so it is excluded. Crash-row counts also vary from 47,024 in 2013 and 50,851 in 2015 to 22,785 in 2024 and 24,303 in 2025; the casualty count is not adjusted for changes in the number of crash records.
